title: Transport milling and reclaiming equipment
intro: Transport is a planned operation involving machine configuration, carrier capacity, route and load securement. The person driving the carrier and the person moving the machine need a shared plan and clearly assigned responsibilities.

sections.title: Describe roles and responsibilities
sections.text: The carrier/driver checks legal loading, axle and vehicle ratings, route/permit requirements and cargo securement within their role. The designated machine operator follows the OMM loading procedure. A trained ground guide controls the agreed communication from a safe position. Do not assume a job title automatically authorizes loading. Confirm who checks ramp suitability, machine mass/configuration, attachments and final securement before movement.

sections.title: Prepare machine for transport
sections.text: Prepare the machine in its specified transport configuration: conveyor, guards, attachments, locks and loose items. Remove attachments only with the approved handling method and rated lifting/rigging equipment where required. Know the actual mass, dimensions and centre-of-gravity implications of fitted equipment. Use designated tie-down points; a convenient handrail or hydraulic line is not one. Secure detached items as separate cargo. Retain guards needed for safe loading.

sections.title: Describe loading and unloading procedures
sections.text: Inspect the carrier, ramps, approach and ground for capacity, support, alignment and traction. Establish a controlled area and agreed stop signal. Follow the machine’s direction, speed and configuration requirements when crossing changes in slope. Stop if a guide is lost or alignment becomes uncertain. After positioning, apply parking/support requirements and the compliant securement system. National Safety Code Standard 10 and applicable BC rules govern the arrangement; chain count alone does not prove adequate restraint. At unloading, control the machine before releasing restraints in the authorized sequence.

worked.title: A mass record that excludes attachments
worked.case: The transport plan lists a base machine mass of 19,800 kg. A fitted conveyor option and attachments add 1,250 kg.
worked.solution: Planned machine load is at least 21,050 kg before any other cargo. Confirm actual configuration, carrier/ramp/axle ratings and route requirements. The base-machine figure is insufficient for release; obtain the transport lead’s verified plan.

activities.prompt: A carrier’s fictional available payload is 22,000 kg. Machine plus attachments is 21,050 kg and separate equipment is 1,200 kg. Find the excess.
activities.answer: Total 22,250 kg, exceeding available payload by 250 kg. Hold and revise the load plan; also check axle distribution and all other limits.
activities.title: A carrier’s fictional available payload is 22,000 kg

activities.prompt: List information needed before selecting tie-downs.
activities.answer: Actual machine mass/configuration, designated attachment points, restraint arrangement, rated components and condition, applicable Standard 10/BC requirements, carrier points and manufacturer transport instructions.
activities.title: List information needed before selecting tie-downs.

activities.prompt: During loading the guide disappears from view. What happens next?
activities.answer: Stop safely, maintain the machine’s controlled state, re-establish the guide’s safe position and communication, then resume only after confirmation. Do not continue from memory of the route.
activities.title: During loading the guide disappears from view

practical: Verify roles, carrier/ramp suitability and transport configuration.
Prepare attachments and approved tie-down points.
Demonstrate controlled loading preparation and final securement checks within the planned time without rushing safety.
